name: Trade war & tariffs
value: Trump threatens to double Mexico tariffs
summary: Trump threatened on 12 Nov to double tariffs on Mexico over a migrant caravan; US–China truce runs to 10 Jan 2027
state: On 12 Nov President Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexican goods immediately unless Mexico stops a migrant caravan that set out from Tapachula on 10 Nov; the two countries are negotiating a trade deal (BNN Bloomberg). On 9 Nov China extended its suspension of some rare-earth, battery and graphite export controls and countermeasures to 10 Jan 2027 (S&P Global). Watch is kept: a major new tariff has been threatened and the US–China truce is short-term.
for_you: Importers and manufacturers trading with Mexico and China face uncertainty over costs and supply, which tends to affect prices and investment plans.
rubric_hit: New major tariff threatened between large economies: US threat to double Mexico tariffs, 12 Nov (Watch)

sources.title: BNN Bloomberg — Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico if it does not halt migrants
S&P Global — China extends rare earth export suspension to January 2027

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
